paragraphs.title: The Allegory of the Two Sisters

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “there were two women, the daughters of one mother.”
easy.q: How many women are described in the allegory?

easy.explanation: The names given are Aholah and Aholibah.
easy.q: What were the names of the two sisters?

answers: They were daughters of one mother
They were daughters of different kings
medium.explanation: The Lord calls them “the daughters of one mother.”
medium.q: What relationship did the two sisters have?

medium.explanation: Aholah represents Samaria, and Aholibah represents Jerusalem.
medium.q: What do the two sisters represent?

medium.explanation: The statement describes their relationship and belonging to the Lord.
medium.q: What does the statement “they were mine” show?

answers: They were daughters of one mother
challenge.explanation: Having one mother symbolizes a relationship between the two kingdoms.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes that the allegory concerns two related kingdoms?

answers: Samaria is Aholah, and Jerusalem Aholibah
challenge.explanation: The verse directly explains the symbolic identities of the sisters.
challenge.q: Which phrase explicitly identifies Aholah with Samaria and Aholibah with Jerusalem?

answers: The allegory concerns only a private family
They represent communities with succeeding generations
challenge.explanation: The sons and daughters reinforce the representation of kingdoms and their peoples.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement that they “bare sons and daughters”?

easy.explanation: Aholah doted upon the Assyrians, while also retaining her former Egyptian associations.

answers: They took her sons and daughters and slew her with the sword
easy.explanation: The Assyrians took her children and killed her with the sword.
easy.q: What did the Assyrians eventually do to Aholah?

answers: She turned to the Assyrians and their idols
medium.explanation: She committed whoredoms with the Assyrians and defiled herself with their idols.

answers: Trusting foreign powers eventually brought punishment through those powers
medium.explanation: Aholah relied upon the Assyrians, and they became the agents of her judgment.
medium.q: What lesson is shown by the sequence in verses 5–10?

answers: The nations and powers to which she turned
medium.explanation: The word refers figuratively to the foreign peoples whose favor and support she sought.
medium.q: In this passage, who were Aholah's “lovers”?

answers: Dependence on and sinful alliances with foreign nations
challenge.explanation: She retained her Egyptian sins and also turned to Assyria and its idols.
challenge.q: What repeated sin appears in Aholah's relations with both Egypt and Assyria?

answers: The power she trusted became the instrument of her punishment
She married the king of Assyria
challenge.explanation: The Lord delivered her into the hand of the Assyrians upon whom she doted.
challenge.q: How did Aholah's relations with Assyria contribute to her end?

answers: She became famous among women after judgment was executed
challenge.explanation: Becoming famous among women in this context refers to the public notoriety of her judgment and disgrace.
challenge.q: Which detail in verse 10 emphasizes that her punishment was public and humiliating?

paragraphs.title: Judah Imitates Samaria and Turns to Babylon

easy.explanation: The text says, “her sister Aholibah saw this.”
easy.q: Who saw the sins of Aholah?

easy.explanation: Aholibah doted upon the Assyrians, her neighbors.
easy.q: To whom did Aholibah first turn in this passage?

easy.explanation: She sent messengers to the Chaldeans, and the Babylonians came to her.
easy.q: To whom did Aholibah turn afterward?

medium.explanation: She was more corrupt and increased her whoredoms beyond those of her sister.
medium.q: What did Aholibah do in comparison with her sister's sins?

answers: She saw images of Chaldean men portrayed on the wall
Aholah commanded her to do so
medium.explanation: When she saw the images of the Chaldeans, she sent messengers to them.
medium.q: What led Aholibah to turn toward Babylon?

answers: Men pictured or depicted on the wall
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to images or paintings displayed on the wall.
medium.q: What does “men pourtrayed upon the wall” mean?

answers: Both sisters followed the same sinful course
Both had the same capital city
challenge.explanation: The statement shows that both kingdoms followed the same general path of unfaithfulness.
challenge.q: What does the statement “they took both one way” emphasize?

answers: Former sinful connections continued to influence her
She became more faithful to God
challenge.explanation: Her remembrance shows that the earlier Egyptian associations had not truly been abandoned.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Aholibah remembering the days of her youth in Egypt?

answers: She saw her sister, turned to Assyria and Babylon, and remembered Egypt
She rejected every foreign nation and remained alone
She turned only to Egypt and conquered it
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from observing Aholah to pursuing Assyria and Babylon, then recalling Egypt.
challenge.q: What sequence best summarizes Aholibah's conduct in these verses?

easy.explanation: The Lord raises up the very nations to which she had turned.
easy.q: Whom does the Lord raise up against Aholibah?

answers: Chariots, wagons, wheels, buckler, shield, and helmet
easy.explanation: The passage describes a fully equipped army surrounding her.
easy.q: With what equipment did the nations come against Aholibah?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Thou shalt drink of thy sister's cup.”
easy.q: Which cup was Aholibah commanded to drink?

answers: The Lord raised them up against her
She invited them to a feast
medium.explanation: God brought against her the powers in which she had trusted.
medium.q: Why did the nations who had been Aholibah's lovers become instruments of judgment?

answers: Siege, stripping, death, exile, and destruction
medium.explanation: The passage describes military judgment, loss, death, and humiliation.
medium.q: What results of judgment are described in these verses?

answers: A cup of judgment and desolation
medium.explanation: The cup symbolizes the severe punishment and ruin coming upon her.
medium.q: What does “the cup of astonishment and desolation” represent?

answers: Judah would bear a punishment like the punishment Samaria received
challenge.explanation: The comparison shows that Judah followed her sister's way and would share a similar judgment.
challenge.q: What is the significance of comparing Aholibah's cup with Samaria's cup?

answers: Forgetting God and turning to the nations leads to drinking the cup of judgment
challenge.explanation: The judgment is connected with her spiritual unfaithfulness and dependence on foreign nations.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in verses 32–35?

answers: She would be punished by the very nations she had come to hate
She would escape from her enemies
She would choose her own enemies
challenge.explanation: The Lord gives her into the hands of the nations she had rejected after depending on them.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by being delivered into the hand of those from whom her mind was alienated?

paragraphs.title: Religious and Moral Abominations and the Lesson

easy.explanation: They committed adultery with idols and defiled themselves with them.
easy.q: What religious sin is charged against both kingdoms?

easy.explanation: The passage says they defiled God's sanctuary and profaned His sabbaths.
easy.q: What did the two kingdoms profane?

answers: Ye shall know that I am the Lord God
easy.explanation: The chapter ends with the declaration, “ye shall know that I am the Lord God.”
easy.q: What final lesson is stated at the end of the chapter?

answers: They caused their sons to pass through the fire for their idols
They sent them to study in Egypt
They hid them in the sanctuary
medium.explanation: They caused their children to pass through the fire to be devoured for their idols.
medium.q: What terrible act did they commit concerning their children?

answers: After sacrificing their children to idols, they came that same day to profane God's sanctuary
medium.explanation: The verses deliberately place the idolatrous sacrifice and the profaning of the sanctuary side by side.
medium.q: How are their religious practices connected with profaning the sanctuary?

medium.explanation: The word refers to their morally and religiously detestable acts.
medium.q: What does the word “abominations” describe in this context?

answers: Idolatry, bloodshed, child sacrifice, profaning the sanctuary, and dependence on foreign nations
challenge.explanation: The chapter describes religious, moral, and political unfaithfulness.
challenge.q: Which combination of sins is presented in the chapter?

answers: To judge them as adulteresses and women who shed blood
challenge.explanation: The righteous judges are to judge them for adultery and bloodshed.
challenge.q: Why are righteous men appointed to judge the two sisters?

answers: To cause lewdness to cease, warn others, and bring knowledge of the Lord
To increase their dependence on foreign nations
challenge.explanation: The punishment is intended to stop their wickedness, teach other women, and bring recognition of the Lord.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the punishment according to verses 48–49?
